source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Skybox Chicago I occupies 190,000 square feet of technical space in Elk Grove Village, Illinois. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this campus, so no power capacity can be stated, and without a power figure no rack or accelerator estimate is meaningful to attempt. The single published certification is LEED, which qualifies the building as meeting a green construction and efficiency standard, and says nothing about uptime tier or suitability for any particular workload class.

Because no IT load figure is published, this site cannot rank Skybox Chicago I against the six Illinois facilities that do publish megawatts, which together account for 236 MW across those six sites. The state context maps 44 facilities in Illinois in total, meaning the large majority publish no capacity number at all, and this campus is one of them. Floor area alone places it among the larger footprints on record, but floor area without power is an incomplete signal for AI infrastructure planning.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the honest answer is that the published record does not yet support a judgment. The 190,000 square feet of technical space is substantial, but AI suitability turns on power density, redundancy tier, and cooling infrastructure, none of which Skybox has published for this location. Until a power figure appears, this campus sits in the same category as the majority of Illinois facilities this site has mapped: present on the map, not yet legible as an AI asset.
